title: Horizon Health rapid onramp brief
body:
One-line summary:
Rapid onramp playbook for Horizon Health: 4-week POC to validate Redwood Hosted API + optional Dedicated routing for clinical note summarization and secure embeddings for search.

Context and objective:
- Horizon Health (clinical documentation SaaS) wants a low-latency summarization endpoint to generate SOAP-style notes from raw visit transcripts and an embeddings pipeline for provider search.
- Primary outcome: demonstrate consistent sub-350ms p95 generation latency for 512-token prompts on Dedicated capacity (or hosted with fallback) and embedding recall >= 0.82 on a curated testset of 200 queries.
- Secondary outcome: show secure data handling pattern (PII redaction + KMS integration) that meets their security checklist so they can evaluate Private deployment later.

High-level scope (what this POC will and won't do):
Will do:
- Integrate a minimal API proxy from Horizon dev environment to Redwood hosted endpoints (with token scoping).
- Deploy a sample dedicated pool (2x A100) for controlled runs and canary fallbacks to hosted model with traffic shaping.
- Run an evaluation harness (200-case testset) for summarization quality + embedding retrieval tests.
- Demo console dashboards: per-route latency, token cost, and rollout controls.
Won't do in this sprint:
- Full on-prem installation or VPC peering (may be scoped in Private follow-up).
- Custom model training or heavy data ingestion pipelines.

Success criteria (explicit, measurable) - must pass all to be considered a success:
1) Performance:
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token sequences on dedicated pool under synthetic load (3 qps steady-state).
- Throughput: system sustains 50 concurrent active users simulated (mix of small/long prompts) with tail latencies < 1s.
2) Quality:
- Summarization ROUGE-L improvement: average ROUGE-L >= 0.58 vs baseline (their in-house summarizer) on 200-case testset.
- Embedding recall@10 >= 0.82 on the curated search testset.
3) Security & compliance:
- Demonstrate KMS-managed key encryption for data at rest and in transit in the POC environment.
- PII scrubbing pipeline applied pre-send with 95% detection rate on seeded PII cases.
4) Operational readiness:
- Console exposes per-route cost and latency; token-level billing reconciliation within 10% of simulated estimates.
- Canary rollback works: configured canary for 10% traffic for 24h and automatic fallback triggers on >=2 SLO breaches.

Acceptance tests (technical):
- Smoke: send sample transcript -> receive structured SOAP note within 500ms for typical 120-token prompt.
- Load: run k6 load script (provided) for 30 minutes at 3 RPS and capture metrics; p95 must meet performance goal.
- Embedding pipeline: ingest 10k anonymized docs, run vectorization, execute 200 queries and verify recall/latency.
- Security: verify that keys are rotated using customer KMS mock and that logs show no raw transcript payloads persisted in Redwood logs (audit).

Workshop / kickoff agenda (90 minutes) - working workshop on day 0:
- 0-10m: Introductions and POC goals alignment (SE + Infra + Horizon PM + Security)
- 10-25m: Data & security walk-through (what example transcripts look like, PII risks, legal checklist)
- 25-45m: Architecture proposal (proxy, token scoping, dedicated pool config) + diagram review
- 45-60m: Ops and monitoring demo (console tour, alerts, rollouts)
- 60-80m: Acceptance criteria & testset review (agree on test vectors, metrics)
- 80-90m: Next steps, action items, and owners

Pre-kickoff checklist (customer-side):
- Provide sample transcripts (200 de-identified cases + 20 PII-seeded cases) by D+3.
- Provide list of compliance contacts and KMS test credentials (or a KMS staging account) by D+5.
- Confirm allowed IP ranges for temporary ingress (if using Dedicated preview).

Pre-kickoff checklist (Redwood-side):
- Provision dedicated pool (2x A100 reserved) in US-West for week 1 testing.
- Prepare k6 load script, eval harness repo (link attached), and initial model config with quantization profile.
- Create a limited-scope service account and scoped API key for Horizon test runs.

Deployment plan & timeline (4-week cadence):
- Week 0 (kickoff): workshop, sample data received, infra prep.
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests. First latency baseline.
- Week 2: run full eval harness (quality + embeddings). Tune batching and kv-cache settings.
- Week 3: canary run with 10% traffic, cost monitoring. Security checklist validation.
- Week 4: review, handoff doc, optional Dedicated reservation proposal and next steps.

Risk register (concise):
- Data sensitivity risk: mitigation = strict PII redaction + ephemeral storage + audit log review.
- Latency miss on hosted: mitigation = adjust routing to Dedicated and tune batching, enable async streaming for long tails.
- Model quality below threshold: mitigation = run temperature sweeps, prompt engineering + small regen policy.
- Infra quota delays: mitigation = prebook GPU capacity and confirm with infra lead (Owen).

Runbook snippets (for on-call during POC):
- Alert: p95 generation latency > 450ms for 15m -> action: scale up dedicated pool by 1 node and notify SE channel.
- Alert: failure rate > 3% -> action: diagnose model errors, check KV cache miss patterns, rollback to previous model tag.
- Manual rollback: use console route-level rollout to shift 100% traffic to hosted fallback and open incident ticket.

Customer responsibilities summary:
- Provide representative data and compliance signoff for test dataset.
- Maintain contact availability for security and network setup during week 0-1.

Redwood responsibilities summary:
- Deliver infra, monitoring, and evaluation harness; implement PII redaction pattern and KMS integration demo.
- Produce final POC report with metrics, cost breakdown, and recommendations for Dedicated vs Private.

Open questions to resolve in first 48 hours:
- Does Horizon require VPC peering or is HTTPS proxy permitted for POC? (owner: Horizon infra)
- Are there internal retention windows (logs/metrics) that would conflict with our eval data plan? (owner: Horizon security)
- Edge case: acceptable semantic drift tolerance for summarization (owner: Horizon PM)

Artifacts we will hand off at close:
- POC report (performance + quality + cost + security checklist)
- Eval harness repo + test vectors
- Console snapshot (dashboards + alerts config)
- Recommendation memo: Dedicated sizing and monthly cost estimate for 99% traffic profile

Immediate next steps (assign owners):
- Priya: schedule kickoff workshop and prepare demo account (by D+2).
- Marco: provision GPU pool and share access (by D+3).
- Horizon: share test vectors and KMS testing creds (by D+3).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep prompts small at first, try n-gram overlap tests to catch hallucination patterns.
- Consider early prefix caching for repeated clinical templates (expected latency wins).
- Watch for token cost explosion on regen-heavy flows; set a token budget alert.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05 initial draft by Priya
- 2025-11-08 added security checklist and k6 script link (Marco)
- 2025-11-12 updated success metrics and timeline (Leah)
